label: Lipoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Most common soft tissue tumor, primarily subcutaneous, under 5 cm.
- Histologically composed of mature adipocytes without atypia.
- Located in the upper back, proximal extremities, and abdomen.
- Deep-seated lipomas necessitate exclusion of MDM2 amplification.
- Rare retroperitoneal lipomas may occur with cytogenetic and molecular confirmation [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html).

## Terminology
- Lipoma: Benign tumor composed of mature adipocytes.
- Intramuscular lipoma and chondrolipoma are recognized subtypes.
- No outdated or synonymous terms [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html).

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Homogeneous mature adipocytes [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Lipoma.html).
  - No atypical stromal cells or hyperchromasia.
- **Desirable:**
  - Absence of MDM2 amplification in deep-seated variants.
  - Presence of fat necrosis or dystrophic calcification.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Reactivated expression of HMGA2 protein in some lipomas [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Most common mesenchymal tumor in adults. Slight male predominance [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).
- **Site:**
  - Commonly subcutaneous in the upper back, proximal extremities, and abdomen.
  - Intramuscular lipomas often occur in the thigh (40-50%) [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html).
- **Presentation:**
  - Painless subcutaneous mass, possibly multiple in 5% of cases.
  - Associated with obesity and specific syndromes like Cowden syndrome [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).

## Macroscopic
- Grossly homogeneous yellow cut surface.
- Well-circumscribed, encapsulated mass [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).

## Microscopic
- Composed of sheets of mature adipocytes.
- May show fibrous septa but lack atypical features.
- Certain variants like osteolipoma include metaplastic bone [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/ENDO/Lipoma.html).
  - ![Histological sections showing a homogeneous population of mature adipocytes.](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_PICS/BST/5372.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **Molecular/Genetics:**
  - Exclusion of MDM2 amplification in higher-risk locations (retroperitoneal/deep-seated) [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html).

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Atypical Lipomatous Tumour/Well-Differentiated Liposarcoma:**
  - Contains atypical stromal cells and MDM2 amplification.
- **Spindle Cell Lipoma:**
  - Contains spindle cells and ropey collagen, with CD34+ staining [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).
- **Angiolipoma:**
  - Presence of vascular channels, clinically painful.
- **Hibernoma:**
  - Multivacuolated cells resembling brown fat, S100 positive [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/softtissueadiposelipoma.html).
- **Myofibroblastoma:**
  - May overlap with spindle cell lesions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html).
- **Desmoid-type fibromatosis:**
  - Overlaps with spindle cell lesions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html).
- **Fat-forming or Lipomatous Solitary Fibrous Tumour:**
  - Differentiation within spindle cell lesions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html).
- **Silicon Granuloma, Signet-ring Cell Carcinoma, Balloon Cell Melanoma, PEComa:**
  - Less common entities within differential diagnosis [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/CYTO_SOFTTISSUE/Lipoma.html).

## Additional Information
- Synovial lipomatosis (lipoma arborescens) is associated with chronic joint disease, lacking HMGA2 overexpression [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/BST/Lipoma.html).

cards.title: Lipoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Lipoma Section: localization Lipomas are most common in the upper back, proximal extremity, and abdominal region, and the majority present as a superficial (subcutaneous) soft tissue mass. A smaller subset are deep-seated, arising within skeletal muscle (intramuscular lipoma), on the surface of bone (parosteal lipoma), or within the tendon sheath, or they may involve the gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, or bronchial tree. Intramuscular lipomas most frequently involve the thigh (40–50%), followed by the shoulder, chest wall, and upper limb. Rare examples of retroperitoneal lipomas with cytogenetic and molecular confirmation have also been reported. Synovial lipomatosis (lipoma arborescens) is a lipomatous proliferation of subsynovial connective tissue often associated with chronic joint disease, and recent work has shown that this adipocytic proliferation lacks HMGA2 overexpression, supporting a non-neoplastic reactive process.

Spindle cell lipomas overlap with other spindle cell lesions of the soft tissue (e.g. myofibroblastoma and desmoid-type fibromatosis) and fat-forming or lipomatous solitary fibrous tumour. cards.title: Myolipoma — Sites
cards.excerpt:
Myolipomas are usually deep seated, with the retroperitoneum being the most common location, followed by the pelvic cavity and abdomen (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:153)
Rare locations include subcutaneous tissue of trunk and head / neck, orbit, nose, tongue, breast, pericardium, spinal - intramedullary and anus (Graefes Arch Clin Exp Ophthalmol 1998;236:630)

cards.title: Myolipoma — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:
Often asymptomatic
Occasionally discovered incidentally by computed tomography (CT) or during abdominal surgery
It may cause pain or discomfort if large or compressing adjacent structures (Diagn Interv Radiol 2010;16:227)

cards.title: Myolipoma — Diagnosis
cards.excerpt:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) shows heterogeneous mass, predominantly with fat intensity
Biopsy reveals mature fat cells interdigitating with smooth muscle cells that lack cytologic atypia

cards.excerpt:

< 10% of cases occur in women
Uncommon compared with conventional lipoma (ratio = 1:60)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Sites
cards.excerpt:
Mostly superficial, extremely rare in deep soft tissue
80% arise in the subcutaneous tissue of the posterior neck, back and shoulders (Cancer 1975;36:1852, Cancer 1981;47:126)
20% involve different sites, including face, oral cavity and trunk / extremities (Acta Pathol Microbiol Scand A 1976;84:477, Histopathology 1987;11:803, Histopathology 2015;66:430, Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487)
Cases in women more likely to arise in atypical locations (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1267)
Intramuscular and dermal based lesions rarely seen (Am J Clin Pathol 2016;146:487, Am J Dermatopathol 2000;22:496)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Characterized by partial or whole chromosome 13 or 16 deletions (Histopathology 1997;31:222)
Breakpoints cluster around 13q14 where the RB1 gene resides (Int J Cancer 2003;103:616)
Part of the so called 13q / RB1 family of tumors, which includes myofibroblastoma and cellular angiofibroma (Hum Pathol 2012;43:1887, Am J Surg Pathol 2016;40:3617, Mod Pathol 2011;24:82)

cards.title: Spindle cell / pleomorphic lipoma — Myxoid background with mast cells frequent
cards.excerpt:
Short and stubby spindle cells show occasional palisading
Rare lipoblasts present in half of cases (Hum Pathol 2017;65:140)
Infiltrative growth, necrosis, atypical spindle cells, pleomorphic lipoblasts and significant mitotic activity usually absent (Semin Diagn Pathol 2019;36:105)
Fat poor and fat free subtype: contains little (< 5%) to no fat (Am J Dermatopathol 2007;29:437, Am J Dermatopathol 2009;31:423)
Myxoid subtype: contains abundant myxoid stroma (Pathol Int 2014;64:346)
(Pseudo) angiomatous subtype: contains dilated endothelial lined channels and nodules of floating tumor (Histopathology 1994;24:565, Pathol Int 2007;57:26)
Plexiform variant has been described (Histopathology 1995;27:533)
Focal cartilaginous and osseous metaplasia rarely present (Histopathology 1987;11:803)
Extramedullary hematopoiesis may occur (Histopathology 2001;39:215)

cards.title: Lipoblastoma / lipoblastomatosis — Mostly occurs in trunk and extremities
cards.excerpt:
